hints.title: Cross Product of Three Schools
hints.text: Every triplet contains one student from SchoolA, one from SchoolB, and one from SchoolC.

hints.title: Pairwise Distinct Conditions
hints.text: All three students must have pairwise distinct student_ids and pairwise distinct student_names.

hints.title: Projection of Members
hints.text: select a.student_name as member_A, b.student_name as member_B, c.student_name as member_C.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT a.student_name AS member_A,
       b.student_name AS member_B,
       c.student_name AS member_C
FROM SchoolA a
CROSS JOIN SchoolB b
CROSS JOIN SchoolC c
WHERE a.student_id <> b.student_id
  AND a.student_id <> c.student_id
  AND b.student_id <> c.student_id
  AND a.student_name <> b.student_name
  AND a.student_name <> c.student_name
  AND b.student_name <> c.student_name;
```

variables: A, B, C: students in respective schools
complexity.notes: Evaluates Cartesian product across all three schools with pairwise inequality checks.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Neglecting name checks or id checks allows students with identical names or duplicate ids into the delegation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Explicit cross join filters out invalid tuples via relational engine optimization.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Multi-table cross join with comprehensive pairwise inequality predicates.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_valid_triplets(school_a: pd.DataFrame, school_b: pd.DataFrame, school_c: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ab = school_a.merge(school_b, how='cross', suffixes=('_a', '_b'))
    abc = ab.merge(school_c, how='cross')
    abc = abc.rename(columns={'student_id': 'student_id_c', 'student_name': 'student_name_c'})
    cond = (
        (abc['student_id_a'] != abc['student_id_b']) &
        (abc['student_id_a'] != abc['student_id_c']) &
        (abc['student_id_b'] != abc['student_id_c']) &
        (abc['student_name_a'] != abc['student_name_b']) &
        (abc['student_name_a'] != abc['student_name_c']) &
        (abc['student_name_b'] != abc['student_name_c'])
    )
    res = abc[cond][['student_name_a', 'student_name_b', 'student_name_c']]
    return res.rename(columns={
        'student_name_a': 'member_A',
        'student_name_b': 'member_B',
        'student_name_c': 'member_C'
    })
solutions.approach: Pandas Cross Merge with Vectorized Filtering
